utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Right. For Your Honours' reference, that's the house marked 202.5 on this witness's exhibit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look at P233, can you explain to the Court what that is a picture of?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: This is a photograph I took on the 26th of April, having been sent back into Ahmici for subsequent patrolling, and it's the same house as that in the previous exhibit. This is the same doorway and this is the room where we attended the woman's needs. You can see again the Rayburn cooker and the breeze block building on the left-hand side of the house, and the fence as well is quite prominent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that it is recorded in the transcript, can you describe the damage to the house?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Well, clearly it had been set alight, either by fire or some incendiary device, removing it of all its timbers, leaving the brickwork. You can probably just see beneath that branch the number 43, which confirms, for the record, that it is actually the very same house, although the other factors, like the cooker and the walls and the wall here clearly also show that that is the same house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that house was destroyed between the 16th and the 26th?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: This house that the civilian woman lived in was destroyed between the 16th and the 26th of April for some extraordinary reason.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This woman was taken away from the house, was she?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: She was, yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was she taken away in an ambulance?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: In an armoured ambulance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was she the only civilian that was taken away in that ambulance?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: That's right, yes, she was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After leaving that house, I think you said you stayed at that house for approximately an hour?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: About an hour, yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go from there?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: I then drove back down the road from which we had come up on our way out of Ahmici, but, of course, I only travelled some 300 or 400 metres before I came across another house where a woman coaxed me to help her.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I would ask that Exhibit 229, the aerial photograph, be placed on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With a pencil, could you briefly describe the route you took from the house where the woman was shot or where the injury was to where you went?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: This is the house where the woman was shot, and we then drove back down this narrow part of the road past a very prominent religious building here onto this slope here where, from the house marked IV, in Roman numerals, a woman coaxed me from sort of the leeside of the building, that is, the sort of northern side of it, to come and assist her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think I've just misled you a little bit a moment ago. It's not the house where the woman was shot, it was the house where you attended to the woman with the injury; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: House number 202.5.

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: 202.5 is the house where the woman had been shot in the head, the elderly woman, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know whether the woman was, in fact, shot?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Well, I think that the injuries were consistent with something like a gunshot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think I've --

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I think I've led this misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know where, in fact, she received the gunshot wound?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: I subsequently heard that she had received the gunshot down the hill, somewhere down the hill, and she had been carried by her family or friends up the hill to her house where she was then under cover.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When you arrived at this next house, the house marked 70 on the aerial photograph, can you explain what the woman -- a woman said to you and what you did after that?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Yeah. Her gestures really said it all in that she needed help quite urgently, and the background of our two previous incidents led me just to follow her and go into the back of the house, if you like, the cellar of the house, where the group of people in the cellar led me to just continue my actions; in other words, I didn't actually necessarily have a conversation with her, neither personally or with any interpreter, because the injured people in the back of the house led me to continue my actions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how many people were in that cellar and what was the atmosphere like in the --

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: The cellar was very dark; there was no lighting. There was an awful smell generally of, I suppose, wounds, and there was also smoke from people smoking. There were crying children, there was a woman breast-feeding, there were elderly people, children, and women, and there was about up to 30 people probably in the cellar, five of whom had significant injuries.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you do anything about those wounds?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Yes. The one nearest the door was a small girl who I believe was about 12 or 13 years old. She had injuries on her left leg, on the lower limb of her left leg, and an injury on the inside of her thigh, on her right thigh, which again I -- were consistent with some sort of, well, an entry wound that I thought was either a low calibre, slow calibre bullet or maybe shrapnel, and we then carried out some first aid of the left lower limb and the right thigh, the inner thigh.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you record that injury in your diary?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Yes. I talked about the injuries.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned the injury of the young girl. Can you explain the other injuries of the others?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Yes. The other one was in the far left-hand corner of the cellar, it was an elderly gentleman, and he, when we tried to move him -- well, he was screaming because -- whenever we tried to move him because of the pain, but it was something like a pelvis or a hip injury, somewhere in his midriff that he was injured either through shrapnel or more probably gunshot wounds.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the other three?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: The other -- the third man -- sorry, the third was a man, an elderly man who had got a gunshot wound to the -- if I recall correctly, the left shoulder, up in this sort of region here (indicating), and those three were the most significant, and therefore we evacuated them in the back of the Warrior, which has got space for infantry personnel. There were two others, and I think they were both men, who had other sort of smaller injuries. We didn't manage to evacuate them in the end.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you record that in your diary as well?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Yeah, I talked about five people being significantly injured from this cellar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Court the average age of these men and what they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: They were wearing civilian clothing, they were anywhere between maybe 45 and 65 years old. There was not many men anyway, but they were of that age. The rest were women and children and elderly women as well, and, you know, even children or, should I say, babies of breast-feeding age. All very scared, all very shocked in this dingy, dark cellar where they were taking cover.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of the men that you saw, these men that were injured, did any of them have weapons?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Not in the cellar, no, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how long did it take you to tend to all of these injuries?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Probably about a further hour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was any drug given to any of these men?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Yes. The man in the -- the second man I talked about who had the hip-type injury or the midriff injury, we gave him morphine in his thigh because he was in such pain that when we tried to evacuate him or move him, he just yelped and screamed, and therefore, by administering some morphine, it enabled us to then move him using a sleeping bag, one of our own, as a stretcher, and we then put him in the back of the Warrior.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Three -- the most severe casualties went in the Warrior and the other two stayed at the house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to show you a photograph in relation to this location -- or a few photographs, and would you be able to describe that in relation to what you've just described to the Court?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The first photograph is marked 234.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you try and relate that photograph to the incident that you've just referred to and the aerial photograph which you have provided the information?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Okay. In the foreground, you can see these three white boxes. These are the periscopes of my own scimitar vehicle, and I had climbed back onto the vehicle -- having already been in the house, I was climbing back on the vehicle in order to get some more first aid kit. I then took the opportunity to take a photograph as a record. At that time, I had gone forward initially, discovered this, and the Warrior, as we see in the middle of the picture, followed me up. I called it up because we needed some more first aid, as in first aid kit, and here you can see two soldiers who are running to the assistance. The house in question is to the right of this fence, down a slope here, a grass -- a hillside -- a slope, and we've come down the track from House number 2 that we talked about up here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you relate that photograph to the aerial photograph by just replacing the aerial onto the projector?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you put the approximate location where that photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Yeah. That is this house here (indicating). The photograph was taken just on the -- on the slope just off the bend here. Along the edge of that road is where that concrete trellis fence is, and this is the green slope I talked about here, and this is the house where there was a cellar with these 30-odd occupants -- not occupants but injured civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the transcript, you've pointed a location on the main road, the main Ahmici road, in front of the house marked number 70; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Sorry. I've -- yes, that's the house there marked 70. Did I misunderstand your question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your vehicle was parked in the vicinity --

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: It was parked, yes, exactly where that pencil is pointing now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd ask that Exhibits 193, 74, 194 and 195 be produced to the witness? I'd ask that the witness look at Exhibit 193 first. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at Exhibit 193, can you explain to the Court what this picture is of?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: This is of the back of the house. The previous picture had been taken up here on the hillside, and this is -- because we had no further ambulance, the ambulance had been tasked and gone, we then used the back of the Warrior personnel carrier to take these three, the most significantly injured people, and put them in the back. So it's in the back of this house on this, if you like, below-ground-level cellar that all this activity took place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at Exhibit number 74, can you describe that, please?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: This is the girl who had the two injuries I talked about, the inner thigh -- I think you can see just here the injury on the inner thigh where we've bandaged it, and she had an injury on her left leg. She, as you can see by her face, is in quite a lot of distress. I think she was about 12 or 13 years old. Other members of the family, and as you can see, civilians, elderly people, women, and children. This is Lance Corporal Priestly who is giving her some bandages, some civilian here giving some light to the situation, our interpreter who is helping console the girl, and in the background here is the man that had the injury around the waist. Because of our limited resources, we were still dealing with the girl who seemed to be most severely injured. This injury, when Lance Corporal Priestly and I arrived, was still bleeding. This man, we then subsequently attended to and gave him the morphine in order to move him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the other men that you assisted, the other men with injuries, do they appear in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: I can't see them. There was a man toward -- in this direction here sitting to his right, to this man's right-hand side, but I can't see him in that picture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In any event, at this location, I think you mentioned there are about 30 people.

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that in the cellar or in and about, behind the cellar?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: That was in the cellar initially. They were all cowering from what had been taking place, but, of course, our arrival with three armoured vehicles, with our 30-millimetre guns, I'm sure provided them with a degree of confidence, in that they then, a few of them, came out of the back of the cellar. Those sort of more -- slightly younger adults had the confidence to come out and assist and to see what was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you can just briefly describe the atmosphere in this cellar?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Dark, dingy, smoky, frightened people crying, babies crying, people shaking, elderly people shocked, I think disbelief at what had happened with their friends and family, you know, injured in front of them. Helpless is probably the thing, helpless, until we arrived and evacuated them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at Exhibit 194, I think you appear in that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Yes. That's me here. I think I had just come from out of the cellar, and I think we're all looking at one of the injured people being removed and put in the back of the Warrior.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And looking at Exhibit 195?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: This is the young girl on this mattress, makeshift stretcher, being placed into the back of the Warrior, which had reversed up to the house, and as you can see, the people, women, and probably slightly elderly men had had the confidence to come out and watch what was going on to their family and friends.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the Warrior left with the three most serious casualties?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: And Lance Corporal Priestly went with them in order to continue his attendance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you can place the -- if I can ask the usher to place the aerial exhibit on the projector? Can you tell the Court what you did once you left this house?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Once we had dispatched the Warrior fighting vehicle with the three injured people, I then returned from the house here to the road here. In fact, further down the road, about 200 metres, my two scimitars had moved further down to spread out in order that they protect themselves a little bit better. We, having finished our job, having given some army rations to the remaining people in the cellar, then decided that we had done as much as we could, and therefore we returned to the vehicles. However, at that time, there had been a -- this is about quarter to 3.00, 2.45, there had been sort of an increase in the intensity of peripheral gunfire and explosions, and most significantly was, at this time, this house with the arrow and the letter "A" which was fully and freshly ablaze, and because of the surrounding danger, the four of us, and that is the two private soldiers I've discussed and the interpreter and myself, if you like, manoeuvred back in pairs to the vehicles in order to ensure maximum cover and, in fact, such was my awareness of this danger that I hid behind a wall, reluctant to expose myself to any gunfire, and I called or I shouted to the driver of my scimitar vehicle to reverse up and collect us so that we did not have to expose ourselves. But because he had his engine running, he was unable to hear us, and therefore, I dashed about 50 yards, 30, 40, 50 yards, down to the vehicle and jumped in, and then we reversed up and picked the remaining three men. So there was five of us in a turret that was designed for two people taking shelter in this environment which had a burning house and gunfire and what have you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You talk about peripheral gunfire. When you say "peripheral," where do you mean? Outside of the village? Within the village?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: I mean possibly in the village, outside the village as well, but gunfire that was 200 metres or more away. A lot of time the gunfire can echo around buildings in built-up areas, but -- and also in this slightly valley-type area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that when you came out of the house, the vehicles, your vehicles had moved down the road somewhat, and you had to attract their attention to try and take cover in the vehicles. About how long did that take before you were in a more protected position within the vehicle?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: About three, three or four minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a problem with one of the vehicles?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Subsequently. The vehicle that I had got into with the four men was fine and reversed in order to pick them up, but the vehicle in front had some fuel carburettor problem, probably as a result of sitting on the slope for a long time, and it then broke down, it was unable to start; and sitting in the vehicle, we then called for a recovery vehicle to come and collect the scimitar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The two vehicles had to stay together; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Yes. Most of the time they were about a hundred yards apart.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in relation to the map, where were those vehicles whilst you were waiting for assistance with the breakdown?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: For the majority of the time I was sitting in a vehicle just slightly astride the A pointer. In other words, the house ablaze. I've got photographs of me sitting next to a coach, which is astride this house which is ablaze.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that time did you see another house on fire? A house or another building?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: There were lots of houses that were smoking as a result of being on fire previously, but this was the most significant which caught my attention. It could not have done anything other than catch my attention as I sat 20 or 30 yards from it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was this second house --

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: The second house is --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- on that particular map?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: -- is on the pointer with the mark B. The picture that I have of this, it was taken when we were recovered and we made our way down the village, and it was of a house that had been on fire, its remaining timbers blackened by the fire and smoke coming from it. And adjacent to it was a barn, which was fully ablaze. And this is at about 3.00. The most significant thing is that this wooden barn was freshly ablaze, which suggested to me it had only just been set fire to at about 3.00, because wooden barns don't burn for very long.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Than wooden barn is at location about B?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: B, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the other house that was on fire was in location A?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In terms of the state of destruction of the other house or the state of the fire, can you give an estimate of when that would have been set alight?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Well, again, the wood is the bit that burns, and the roof, the timbers, are the bits that burn, and they burn, from my experience, of which I have got quite a bit now, quite quickly. And within the space of my wait in the vehicle, at that point, which was about 40 minutes, the house had been fully ablaze and had burnt out, completely gutting it of its floor, and timbers and roof. The roof had fallen in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would now like to show you some photographs, four photographs, of this particular incident. And can you explain to the court how, in fact, you came into possession of these photographs? How is it that you can provide these to us? Perhaps if you can explain to the Court how you took these photographs.

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: I took them with my own camera on the day in order to keep a log and a record of the situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And other photographs you are referring to in your evidence generally, where would they have come from?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: All the photographs I am aware of were either mine or Corporal Penfound, who was the military photographer whom I went into the village with, and I gave my camera to him to take these pictures.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He followed your route through the village?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: That's right. Up until the point when he went back with the Warrior.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's with the three injured people?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Yes, with the three injured people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honours, as these photographs form a series with other photographs that have been tendered in evidence, I would ask for Exhibit number 137 and 134. Major Woolley, if once the other two exhibits are brought to you, if you could put them in some sort of chronological order as events occurred for you, and then we'll describe each photograph in detail.

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: This is the house which had the arrow with the A pointing to next to the coach I was talking about. And this is the hatch of my own vehicle, and you can see another vehicle behind here. The house quite clearly alight. This is at about 3.00. In the distance you can see what I believe is that religious building I pointed out earlier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you can turn the exhibit over and just state the exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could put the aerial exhibit back on the ELMO and relate, again, where that house is?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Where the arrow A points is the house and just next to it is the track.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's the house marked -- pointing --

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: To A (indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for the record, that's Exhibit P229. And the next photograph. If you can look at the rear and state the exhibit number as well.

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: It's 137. This is a better shot of the house. I think we can see quite clearly how the house is ablaze, the roof is falling in and the timbers are burning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that photograph taken whilst you were stationery?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: That is right, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Show the next exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Exhibit 236. As I've stated, I was only sitting here for about half an hour, and within that time, this is all pivoting around 3.00, the house quite clearly has burnt out, pretty much burnt out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you see the house first ablaze? You've obviously seen it whilst the fire was in full force. Did you see the beginning of that fire?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: I didn't see it being set fire to, but as we advanced across the field it was quite clearly ablaze. And, in fact, I apologise, but I've put this exhibit slightly out of order, because you can see that this is before the house was ablaze. At this point I'm on the vehicle most upward -- most uphill, and I had swapped vehicles when the other vehicle was broken down. The previous pictures you saw were when I was just below this bus, and you can see here the smoke from the house quite clearly. This trellis type concrete fence is the fence that I took cover behind. You can't see it here on the picture. And at that point my vehicle that I'm sitting on now was here and had reversed up with me in order that we picked up the other chaps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the house that was set alight is to the right of the picture, behind that house you see in the foreground?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: That's right. It's just behind here, yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the photographs that have been shown by yourself are photographs taken from the opposite direction --

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- facing up the hill?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the background --

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you can replace that exhibit. In the background to the left, that white structure.

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: That's the minaret of Ahmici, still standing on the 16th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is about 3.00 in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: About 3.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you can state the number of that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you can show the next photograph.

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: This is Exhibit 238. This is from what I believe is roughly the same position. So to the right of this tree we have -- or a bit further up from this tree we have the house that I talked about already on the A pointer. In the distance I can obviously see another light alight, which is on the pointer B, the second house, a white house, very significant -- very clearly you can see a grey drainpipe here, ablaze. That is about it, I think, for that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you driving past this house --

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: I believe this is --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- when that was taken or static?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: I believe this was static at this point. I don't believe I took any pictures while moving.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've stated the exhibit number for that?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Yes. That was 238. Exhibit number 134. This is the same house, a white house, and you can see this grey drainpipe again. Burnt out now. This is all within, as I say, 30 to 45 minutes, and yet this barn to the left-hand side is quite clearly ablaze, freshly ablaze. The reason why I took this picture was because here, on the front doorstep, is a man who appeared to be dead. Well, he was very static anyway, and he'd either had a nasty fall on the steps or had been shot as he exited the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's not so clear from the photograph that that is, in fact, a man. Did you have a better view when you were there?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Well, no better view than that other than the zoom of my the camera, but on the original photograph it's quite clear a man has been killed somehow on the steps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think there's another exhibit that we haven't looked at.

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: I think that's it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have exhibit -- I asked for Exhibit 155.

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Yes. This is, again -- we've obviously moved about 30 metres down the road. This is my vehicle hatch, and the house is burnt out and the barn is still ablaze but shot as significant as it was. And you can see the cars showing it was the same house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any soldiers in and about that area where those houses were alight?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: There were no soldiers around there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go from there? After you saw this burning barn, where did you head?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Soon after this point we were recovered by the engineers who then took us back to Vitez to recover the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whilst you were in Ahmici, you mentioned in a statement that you provided to the Tribunal that you saw, I think, some men with weapons, which you believed to be Muslim. You haven't mentioned them in your testimony. Where did you see -- or did you see any Muslim men with any weapons, and if you did, where did you see them?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: The only men who were Muslim who had weapons, and I know that they were Muslim because they were talking to the Muslim lady who -- and this is the first incident I'm talking about with the injured man, were about four men who were middle-aged, and a couple who were reasonably young, 25 or 6, who were not particularly dressed as soldiers, although I understand that not all soldiers out there were dressed in uniform, and they carried Kalashnikov rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I'd like to show you a photograph, and can you tell the Court what this is a photograph of? We have no photocopies of this, but we can supply them on the break. Black and white for today.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Exhibit 239.

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Yes. If we go back to about 11.00 in the morning, not long after I'd arrived, that is the woman you may recall who last an injured friend or relative in the house. At this point, obviously with my interpreter, with the woman we were discussing issues, and you can see here two young men who have got rifles, who could have been soldiers, although I believe they were sort of a local defence sort of outfit, and another man here, soldier, and one here. And all around that house there were about five men who I would describe as of fighting age. And at this time, you see this woodpile here, there was a small outhouse here, and the two private soldiers, when I was talking here, were then carrying over dead bodies of old men from the front fields just at the T-junction of the main road and delivered them to the outhouse. And I asked what was wrong with them. This is right at the start. I asked, "What is wrong with them?" And he said, "These are dead," which is a small shock.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying dead bodies? Are you saying two or are you saying more than that?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: I remember seeing two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these particular people, Muslims with weapons, were they picking those dead bodies up?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: No, they hadn't bothered. I don't know why. I was distracted by the incident and the woman, and as I was talking, my soldiers had taken it on themselves, I don't know why, but they ended up picking these two bodies up and put them over by the barn.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did these men in the photograph, with rifles, appear to be doing?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: I think they'd been the local defence of the village, and I don't know whether they'd come there as a result of the action in the morning at about 6.00, or whether they had been there, but if there had been action of a military action rather than a civilian slaughter, then I assume they would have been -- while defending their friends and relatives they would have probably been injured or killed themselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And apart from that location, and I think the location you're referring to is marked by number 1 on the map, with the house ringed with the 14 numeral next to it, that is the house where you saw these --

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: That's the very house, yeah, there (indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this is the house where the man was assisted because he had a gun-shot wound to his back?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: To his back and arm, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are there any other locations that you saw Muslim men with weapons, apart from this particular location?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: This is the only one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your impression when you left the village? And this might tie into your impression when you arrived. Did you feel that an action had taken place or were you caught in the middle of one? Can you give the Court some understanding of when the tempo of this action, whatever it was, occurred to cause the damage that you've referred to, the 20 per cent of houses you saw burnt within your field of view along side of the road, what was your impression about when that, in fact, occurred? Do you have one?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: My impression was based, after my arrival, on talking to the woman, and on seeing the injured man and by the nature of his wound in his back, the quantity of blood on the sofa, and the congealed nature of the blood and the abating of the bleeding, although not completely, that he'd probably been there for about three hours, four hours. No less than two, no more than four. Basically these were the things that made me believe -- sort of put a time on it, but also the woman had commented that it was a morning offensive. And most deliberate offensives conducted by military men are done at dawn, because that's the time when the people are at least alertness, probably in their beds.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in relation to what the woman told you, was that consistent with what you saw?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you headed back to the Vitez base; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were in the village for about three or four hours; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Four hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you mentioned there was an increase in gunfire, if not peripheral gunfire, when you were travelling the route or waiting for the vehicle, the recovery vehicle, to fix up one of the vehicles that had broken down. What about the rest of the four hours? What sort of gunfire was heard, if any, during that time?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Again, I'll describe it as peripheral in that I was aware that there was gunfire going on. Whether that was nearby or echoing gunfire I could not specify, but certainly there was gunfire in and around the periphery of the area. But really because of the nature of what we came across, I was more focused on the problem there, and this, I suppose, distracted me from other concerns like the gunfire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But there wasn't any sort of offensive occurring whilst in front of you or near you whilst you were in the village?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: There was no offensive. The only thing that made me believe that some fresh action of sorts had taken place was that a wooden barn and a house -- and, in fact, two houses, were freshly ablaze. They were not ablaze when I entered the village at 11.00, but they were ablaze at 3.00 and burnt out quite quickly. So obviously something had taken place from the sort of western -- north-western edge of the village. Maybe using an approach from the hillside towards further up the hill, or maybe down towards Santici, which is a Croat village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You went back to the Vitez base and then at some later time did you re-attend the village or near to the village?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Yes, we then -- we went back to reorganise ourselves and to change the vehicle that had broken down, and then I was tasked to join Lieutenant Dooley who had spent his afternoon recovering dead bodies, and I assisted him later at about 6.00 in the evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's what he told you he had been doing?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Yes. He'd been doing it since about 12.00 or about midday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you met him, and what time did you -- sorry, I might have missed that, but what time were you back at the village, outside the village?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: At about 6.30. We rendezvoused at Dubravica, at the junction, at about 6.00, and we must have been on the main road, on this road along here, there was four Warrior vehicles and two of my Scimitars, at about 6.30.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see anything of significance when you arrived there, in relation to casualties?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Yes. You'll see the figure 6 with a circle around it. This is an area of a field just on the eastern edge of a house where there were five bodies, civilian and elderly bodies, lying on the grass at what appeared to be where they had fell whilst being shot. In fact, they had several injuries to their bodies. They had not just been shot once from the injuries that I saw. And it was those five bodies that we were tasked to recover. So with four Warriors and with my two Scimitars, we picketed this road to ensure our own safety. Corporal Ramsden, my other Corporal, was at the bottom by this cemetery here, and I placed myself here at the top end by the junction of Ahmici, and the four Warriors were placed along the road here to provide security, so that the armoured ambulance could reverse onto this field as close to the dead bodies as possible in order to collect them and put them in the back of the ambulance. And then our task really was to remove them and take them to the edge of the village so that if any Muslim people wanted to collect them they could do more safely. That was the concept of what we were up to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That circle with the 6 represents the place that you feel that the bodies were located and retrieved from?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Yeah. That's -- by the nature of how they were lying, it appeared that they were lying where they had fell whilst being shot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I produce a few exhibits to you that may assist in describing this incident. They're Exhibits 53, 54, 55, 56 and 57. If we can look at Exhibit 53 first, please.

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: This white block is the periscope of my vehicle, and this is the field. As you can see, the bodies are lying here. This is where the circle that's drawn on the map with the mark 6 is. You can see in the distance some of the smoking buildings of Ahmici. This is the edge of Ahmici, and you can see the destruction of some of these houses. This line along here is the main road, which you can't obviously see, but clearly the dead bodies are there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we look at Exhibit 54?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: This is the -- excuse me. This is the armoured ambulance. These are some Cheshire soldiers taking cover or covering us as we reversed, opened the door and then put the bodies in the back. Here is a dead man, a civilian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Exhibit 55.

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Here is another dead man. And another man next to him here, slightly more -- middle-aged. We were about to pick these bodies up and put them into the back of the ambulance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Exhibit 56.

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: This is the ambulance door and the entrance -- the back of the ambulance, and these are the bodies. There's obviously one, two, and here is the feet of a third. There was a couple more on the stretcher up here. This man I personally lifted into the ambulance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's the man with the purple jacket?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Yes. He's got a bad injury to his arm, and he has a couple of other injuries that suggested to me that he'd probably been engaged with automatic fire or with several sort of single-aimed shots. Probably automatic fire, because after the first shot you tend to fall down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Exhibit 57.

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Here is probably a better view of one, two, three, four, five people. A soldier here with his rubber gloves on. Yep.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I would just like you to describe all of the men. Were any of them in any sort of obvious uniform?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: None of them were in any obvious uniform or any -- my experience was that most Bosnian solders had, if not any uniform, had one or two items of uniform, what I would call mixed dress, but none of these had any green jacket or sleeveless black top or anything signifying anything military whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any weapons next to these --

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: There were no weapons anywhere near them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you've described one or two of the bodies and how you believed they, in fact, were killed. Can you describe the others? Are you in a position to?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: I'm not really in a position to describe them other than they were all dead and they sustained more than one shot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so those bodies were subsequently taken further up the village, I think you said?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Yeah. They were taken to the east -- I shall, if you like, point on the map where we took them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could? And that's pointing on Exhibit 229. If you can mark the location with an X with the red pen of the place where the bodies were taken?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: (Marks). Took them to the small lay-by there just north-east of the cemetery here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you said that you took those bodies to that location so to enable Muslim people to pick these bodies up --

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- in more safety?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to show you another photograph, and if you can explain to the Court what that is? It's a new exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 240.

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: This is -- you can see three of the four Warriors here parked on the road. You can see, between these two Warriors, Corporal Ramsden's scimitar at the end of the road further towards the cemetery, you can see here my vehicle just off the road, and you can also see that the headlights are on -- it's quite -- it's getting dark or getting darker, and we had actually completed the removal of the bodies and we're now on our way. I recall that we had been distracted by gunfire in the Ahmici area, and therefore, you can see these three barrels over to the right-hand side of the decks of the vehicles. Something I also recall -- I have a photograph somewhere, but I can't find it -- of direct fire being shot from this hillside here, which I believe to be a Croat position, it's on the western side of the Busovaca sort of area, Busovaca being further into this valley, and it was a series of tracer rounds with gaps between them. They're obviously automatic, but the gaps between them were consistent with that of something like an anti-aircraft gun being used in the direct role, the surface role of probably 20 or 30 millimetres and sufficiently fast and flat trajectory to tell me that they were of that nature, and they were being fired from the top of this hill across into Ahmici, into the village area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how many firings did you see?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: There were a couple of bursts. In fact, I remember trying to take a picture of them, and every time there was a burst, I managed to -- I failed, and finally caught a picture on the last burst of ammunition of fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any burst back?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Not that I was aware. I didn't see any, not on their return.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With the red marker, could you put the trajectory or what you saw onto that last exhibit, 240?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: (Marks). That's really behind that house but from the top of this hill across, into the back of here. That's in the distance rather than in the foreground. Difficult to show, really.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at that photograph, there's a damaged house that appears to be at the corner of the junction. Did you notice whether that was damaged when you arrived there or left there earlier that day?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: It wasn't damaged when I arrived there, but I didn't notice it on the exit of the village at about 3.30.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it could have been --

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: It could have been done --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- destroyed any time after your arrival?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you put an arrow on the direction of the trajectory for the record on that exhibit on which way --

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Sorry, direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- which direction it was actually heading.

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you put Exhibit 229, which is the aerial of the village, can you explain what the white arrow generally reflects?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Yes. That white arrow is the direction of the fire, and this is actually a hilly feature, which is difficult to see from this two-dimensional picture, but when I took the picture that you've just seen in the last example, I was sitting here (indicating). That house that was destroyed, that we just talked about, is here, the Warriors are lined along here, and Corporal Ramsden and his vehicle down here, and that fire that I saw came across here into the back of Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were only involved in one body pick-up; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But is it your belief that there were other body pick-ups by other people?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: That afternoon, I understood that Lieutenant Dooley had conducted a series of pick-ups something like two or three, of about four to six bodies each time and taken them somewhere. I don't know where.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that pick-up, you headed back to base again?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: That's right, yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how long did that take?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: It was -- I'd say the whole thing wrapped up within about an hour, probably a bit over an hour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at this photograph that I'll produce to you -- it's a new exhibit -- could you explain to the Court what that is?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The exhibit is marked 241.

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: This is a picture of Vitez. You can see the Catholic church here, the Catholic end of -- the Croat end of town, and this is the Muslim end, and if you could see through the smoke, you'd see a minaret around here somewhere. This is my vehicle periscopes, this is -- that's pointing east, that direction. So what we're doing is we're going along the ring road to Dubravica late in the day, although it's not a very good, clear shot. Because we're going east, I understand it to be my second journey to Ahmici that day, so this is not the morning but the second journey to go and pick up the bodies, and as I can see, the area of Vitez is still smoking from its activity that morning or that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's the area I'd like to briefly discuss now, is putting what you saw in Ahmici in some sort of Vitez-wide, municipal-wide context. Did you go into Vitez on the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the route you took was always a ring route around --

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Yeah, the northern route around Vitez. There was no reason for me to go into Vitez and, in fact, the intensity of what was going on in Vitez was the first reason why I was left in a mess in the morning and was only then sent to Ahmici to investigate what apparently at the time was some activity, unspecified.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the 16th of April, did you visit some other villages that had received some substantial damage?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Yes, I did, yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe on the 30th of April, you visited a village called Jelinak?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how far away is that from Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: It's probably -- it's -- if you take a circular route up to the north-east, it is about 8 kilometres, 10 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the predominant population in Jelinak, what --

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: It was a predominantly Muslim village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you go to Jelinak?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Because I was, on the 30th of April, I was handing over my responsibility to a lieutenant from the light dragoons who were the regiment taking over from us in Bosnia, and I visited -- Jelinak is part of routine patrols or a routine handover, although I had never actually been there before. I had been to Putis, which is just east of Jelinak, but then decided to venture into Jelinak with Lieutenant Rennick.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was a general patrol; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: A general patrol as well as a handover patrol.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you pick that particular village?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Just coverage of the area, a random coverage of the area, in some respect, and also more specific coverage of the area with regard Ahmici and other places.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what of significance did you see in that village?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Well, I drove from Putis up into the village to the first house on my left-hand side, and there I stopped when a couple of men came out of the building and asked me to stop, stop to talk to them, and they asked me to jump down and come and look at something, so I decided to jump down, took my rifle with me, and the one soldier, who was a grey-haired man but quite strong-looking, maybe in his late 40s, showed me where three people had been killed and which -- the bodies were still there, or the remnants of the bodies. He showed me against the side of the building, the back of the house, three splotches, three marks of blood where it was very evident three people had been shot. The red marks were at head height, so there had been three men shot in the head. The blood had trickled down the wall, and then where the men had been dragged away onto some grass, there was a trail of blood, congealed blood, you could see the trail to where the bodies then lay. I say "bodies." The first was pretty much a head, charred head, skull, quite easy to recognise as a human skull; the second was a skull and shoulders and a bit of torso, again charred completely; and the third was a full torso and head with absolutely perfect features of a human being and arms other than the fact that they were absolutely jet black as that cloak, having been burned. What was most extraordinary was the fact that next to the black and burnt torso were two knee-length black leather boots, what I've described as jackboots, which had the legs inside them, which were not burnt, which is significant, I think. You could see the bones, the knee bones and the flesh, where they had obviously been chopped off before they had burned the bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were these bodies? Were they in a house? Were they outside?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: They were outside the house next to -- you could follow the blood trail from the three spots on the wall -- I say "spots" -- patches of blood this large trickled down, follow the blood. The three remains of the bodies were outside on the grass on the eastern edge of a house in Jelinak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And about how many houses were in Jelinak; have you got any understanding --

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Jelinak was very stretched out, and it sort of merged into Loncari. It's not a large village, maybe 40 houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any damage to the houses?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: The houses -- typical burnt-out roofs, beams. The roofs had collapsed where they had been set on fire, doorways and windows blackened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What percentage of the village appeared to have been destroyed in that manner?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: I think about 40 or 50 per cent of it had been destroyed, and this is sometime after, and it was absolutely deserted apart from the couple of guys who came from some hide where they had been.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the date in which this destruction occurred and killing?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Well, it can only really -- the last time I was anywhere near there was the 15th of April, on the night when I was in Putis, and I was there then on the 30th of April, so it was anywhere between those two dates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you've got no specific knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: No, although most of the activity I understand went on between the 16th and the 25th of April I understand just from my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This village was predominantly Muslim; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: That's right, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the Serb frontlines in relation to Jelinak, can you explain to the Court where they would be? Would they be nearby?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Well, from Jelinak, the Serb frontline is not even significant, there's no weapon. This was -- in that theatre would be able to be launched from a Serb position, certainly not to the east but to the nearest Serb frontline to the west and north-west was Turbe which was about 20 miles away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Bearing that in mind, what was your presumption as to which military force generally inflicted that damage on that village?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: It was the HVO that had attacked that village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you didn't see the particular attack.

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: This is a Muslim village. Serbs are miles away. Conclusion: Croats attacked this village. There was also some -- there was also two pigs in the village that were still smouldering, in fact, when we arrived there, and I don't think pigs smoulder for 15 days when lit. I think they were put -- I assume they were put there just to desecrate or soil, make a point about Muslim faith, in that they were brought along and destroyed there to sort of desecrate the village, if you like, and they were still smouldering when I arrived there, suggesting they had been lit or shot or something like that only a few days before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the village populated or was it empty?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: It was deserted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's a village near Jelinak called Loncari. You visited that on that --

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- same day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: I arrived in Jelinak from the east along through Putis and I exited Jelinak through Loncari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see in Loncari of significance, if anything?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: It was very similar to Jelinak, really. It was a continuation. Again, houses burnt, blackened timbers, burnt windows and door frames, and livestock -- there's a lot of livestock, horses, and some cattle that had been killed and had -- rigor mortis had set in because their legs were stretched out straight as they were lying on their sides, a general bad smell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give the Court some sort of understanding of the size of the village, how many houses, what type of village was it?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: A rural village, quite a long, thin village. I'm not sure if it didn't follow a small stream, but a linear village, I'd say, maybe of -- between 30 and 50 houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give an estimate of the number of houses that appeared to be in a burnt, destroyed state from which you mentioned earlier?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Probably anything between a quarter and half of the houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any sign of death in that village?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: The animals. Apart from the -- in Loncari -- Jelinak aside and the other three bodies I've talked about -- in Loncari, all I witnessed was dead animals, particularly a horse I remember very clearly, dead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Court the predominant ethnic group that lived in that village?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: I understood the ethnic grouping to be Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This village falls into a similar situation in terms of Jelinak in that it was quite a way away from the Serb frontline, Bosnian Serb frontline; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Yes, very much so, yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what conclusion do you have in relation to the military group or that would have been involved in that attack on that village?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Well, I'm not very clear on the Muslim or Croat intent at the time, their intentions, their concept of operations, but the relevance of taking that village, a Muslim village, so a Croat offensive on that village seemed to bear no relevance, militarily, as there was no fortifications in that village, there were no trenches, there were no sangars or defended houses that I saw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your experience in Bosnia on that tour and your tour following, can you offer another alternative if, in fact, a military group organised an attack on this village of Loncari other than the Bosnian Croat military, apart from a Bosnian Muslim military group?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes, Counsel Radovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think that this has anything to do with the indictment, and I have an objection. For example, the village of Loncari, what has that to do with Ahmici, and the pigs that were mentioned, the slaughtered pigs which were several kilometres from Ahmici and it has nothing to do with this case, and all this happened 15 days later, whereas the indictment concludes with the 16th of April. I think that we were tolerant enough, but I think things have gone too far now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Smith?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: In relation to that, Your Honour, the main focus of this witness's testimony has been Ahmici, and in relation to the crimes against humanity count, we must prove that what occurred in Ahmici was part of a widespread or systematic attack on the civilian population, and that's obviously why it's being led, and as far as the dates of when this village -- these two villages were attacked, the witness didn't say the 30th of April, he said that's, in fact, when he visited, and he believed that the attack on those villages was between the 16th and 25th. In any event, I'm going to be moving off this topic, but it is an important point for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I agree, yes. But you should try to phrase your questions in such a way that they are not leading. Yes, Counsel Radovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I accept this theory, that the indictment would like to prove broader aspects, but for our aspects, for our clients, for them to prove that they were -- a broader aspect, that they should show that they had a higher position in politics or elsewhere. So when they step outside the frameworks of Ahmici, that is, people who had no military or civilian authority, I don't think this comes within the frameworks of the indictment as it stands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Sorry, Counsel Radovic. With all due respect, you are wrong from the viewpoint of international law. You were referring to command responsibility. We are not dealing with the question of command responsibility, we are dealing with the question of whether or not the alleged crimes committed by the accused may be characterised as crimes against humanity. Now, as you know, one of the ingredients of crimes against humanity is that they are part of a widespread practice or systematic practice, whatever the position of responsibility in a command structure of the accused. A rape committed by a soldier may be classified as a crime against humanity if it is part of a widespread practice; so therefore, their position of responsibility is not relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I'm moving off this topic. Just one last question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was -- who do you believe, based on the circumstances that you had at hand, was responsible for the attack on Loncari?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Based on what I saw, on my understanding of the Croat and Muslim dispositions, based on what the woman at the start of the village told my interpreter and therefore me, it was clear that there was an HVO offensive that had taken this village, Muslim village, which had a minaret very clearly standing on the 16th of April at the front of the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, I was referring to Loncari.

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. Again, as a result of my understanding of dispositions, in our operations room, we had a demographic or ethnic chart, and from that, I knew this area to be predominantly Muslim, and it had received destruction of a nature similar to that of Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The civilians had gone from Loncari; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said in the beginning of your testimony that you received training and education in the law of armed conflict, the rules that apply to war. In relation to the principles of protection of civilians and protection of civilian property, can you give the Court an opinion on the nature of the attack, whether you, as an educated, experienced military soldier, believe it was an unlawful operation or the damage and the injuries that you saw was legitimate?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt you. Could you maybe rephrase this question because actually it's not important -- it is for the Court to decide whether it was lawful or unlawful. The question is whether it was a military operation or -- let me see, the words used by the witness. He said there was, in a way, a choice between military action or civilian slaughter. So without classifying the action as lawful or unlawful, whether it was, rather, a military action or a civilian slaughter, to use his own words.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I'm happy with that question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Again, from what I saw, from what I was told by the woman, from the smoking houses, from the smoking civilian houses, the dead -- couple of dead men of what I would describe as non-combatant age, from a man who was in civilian clothing in a jumper who had got a shot in the back, in the back, suggesting he was withdrawing or running away or something, from a woman who saw -- with a very nasty face, who was probably about 50 or 60, a woman with a head wound, which is a gunshot, a single shot on her head, and from a whole cellar of anything from old men to children, a small girl of 12 years old, from seeing that and seeing no defences, only a few men earlier on in the day of combat age with rifles, my impression was that whether there had been any soldiers in this village at all, of which there was only a very, very small example, these few men I've talked about, at the end of the day, these houses, these civilian houses, had been burnt down, were on fire - these were not houses that had any signs of being defended by soldiers or had any fortifications - and I think when you see 12-year-old girls with bullet wounds and even men who could fight with gunshot wounds in their backs or women with gunshot wounds in their heads, it tells me that this is a slaughter of civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour. I apologise for being lengthy with this witness, but because he was very much involved on the day, it does take a little time. I would like to tender Exhibits 229 to 241.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right. So we now take a break, 30-minute break. We will reconvene at 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Pavkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to inform you that the witness will be questioned by counsel Ranko Radovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel Radovic. Cross-examined by Mr. Radovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, Major, as far as I was able to understand, you are an infantry man, or armoured units, or what is your category, in fact? What is your rank?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: I'm from a reconnaissance armoured unit, cavalry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your specialist training -- does artillery come under your specialist training?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Not under my specialist training, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about anti-aircraft guns, is that part of your training too?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: ... I'm trained in, but I have a good all-round knowledge of the all-arms battle, and that includes air defence and artillery, and infantry work and armoured work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see anti-aircraft guns, the ones that the HVO had at their disposal in the surroundings of Vitez, did you personally see them?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: I didn't see the guns, but I saw fire from a gun, from a HVO area, which with its rate of fire, the size of the tracer, the trajectory of the gun, made me understand that they were clearly anti-aircraft guns, and I can further confirm that if you wish me to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know that it was a 30-millimetre anti-aircraft gun?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: I didn't know it was a 30-millimetre gun, I said it was between 20 and 30 millimetres, because anti-aircraft guns are normally anything between 23 millimetres, 20 millimetres, sometimes as little as 12.7 millimetres and sometimes as much as 40. That's why I said between 20 and 30, roughly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Do you know, in concrete terms, what anti-aircraft were against at the disposal of the HVO and the Muslim side, the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: I think most of the units out there had former JNA weapons, and most of these weapons are based on Russian or Soviet type weaponry, the ZPU or ZSU type anti-aircraft guns. Mainly ZPUs, ZPU-4 12.7 millimetre, 20 millimetre, some 23 millimetres and even 57 millimetres in some cases.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I'm now interested in knowing how you decided upon this category between 20 and 30 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: The rounds that were fired over the hillside had firing intervals in that I'm saying the rate of fire showed me that they were, first of all, not machine gun, which puts them in a larger bracket. Okay? They were also not of a rate of -- do you want me to continue, or are you going to talk?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, you can carry on. I can ask you the next question in that regard. Do you know that anti-aircraft guns are conceived in such a way as to have limited possibility for reducing the barrel downwards, just like with tanks, you can't raise the barrel upwards, which is the case with Russian tanks, for example. And this one can't go downwards. Do you know of that fact?

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: That's not correct. You can depress an anti-aircraft gun to fire in a direct role, and in fact, I was fired on by Serb guns in January over near Kladanj, where anti-aircraft guns were fired at me in a direct role from the other side of a valley, and I had this confirmed to me by the Bosnian Serbs when I visited a town over their border some weeks later, and we had a good laugh about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But do you know whether it was the same type of weapon, because I imagine that not all types have the same combat possibilities.

utterances.speaker: MATTHEW ROBERT WOOLLEY
utterances.text: Anti-aircraft guns can fire in the direct role and they can be depressed. It is the simple case of letting a gun lower. They all fire from the horizontal with either a series of hand controls, winches, and they can be elevated up to the vertical and, in fact, beyond it, all around 360 degrees. Because when you're firing at an aircraft, it may be coming towards and you're firing like this, and they're coming up like that and you might be going around and beyond. Soviet anti-aircraft guns fire in all directions, including on a flat trajectory on the horizontal.
